challenges.name: Anchor Streak
challenges.note: Nine correct actions in a row

hazards.frayed-lanyard-hazard: That lanyard has a visibly frayed core strand where it runs over the snap hook — hardware that already looks like this has already taken more load than it should have. Clipping into it trades a fall-arrest device for a length of webbing that only looks like one.
hazards.gate-wedge-hazard: That wedge block is jamming the platform gate open from the last shift's shortcut. A gate that cannot close is a gap in the one rail meant to stop a step backward from becoming a fall off the platform's own open side.
hazards.missing-pin-hazard: That pothole-guard pin socket is empty — the retaining pin that keeps the guard from lifting off the platform's own understructure is missing. A guard that can lift free is a guard that stops protecting the exact moment a wheel finds an uneven seam in the floor.
hazards.quick-release-hazard: That is the quick-release lever that unclips the lanyard without lowering the platform first. A lanyard is only doing its job while the platform is still in the air — a lever built to remove it early removes the only thing standing between a stumble and a fall from height.

interrupts.alert: The platform has tilted slightly to one side as the case shifted — an uneven load on the fork faces.
interrupts.cue: Stop the transfer and report the tilt to the picker radio rather than shifting your own weight to level it.
interrupts.missNote: The tilt was worked around instead of reported. A platform that tilts once under an uneven load will tilt again, and leaning to compensate is how an associate ends up leaning past the rail instead of behind it.
interrupts.why: A platform that tilts under an uneven load is a platform whose fork faces need to be checked before the next lift, and shifting body weight to compensate teaches exactly the wrong reflex — reporting it is what gets the load re-centred by someone looking at the whole picker, not guessed at from inside the harness.
interrupts.wrongNote: Not that — the tilt goes to the picker radio before this transfer continues.

interrupts.alert: An associate has walked into the aisle directly beneath the elevated platform.
interrupts.cue: Sound the horn and hold position. Do not lower the platform until the aisle is clear.
interrupts.missNote: The platform was lowered without sounding the horn. An aisle that was clear a moment ago is not the same thing as an aisle that is clear now.
interrupts.why: Lowering a platform blind onto an aisle that was clear thirty seconds ago assumes nothing has changed underneath it — the horn is what tells the person below to move, and holding position is what keeps this from being the moment a loaded platform comes down onto someone who never knew it was there.
interrupts.wrongNote: Not that — the horn and holding position come before anything else about this descent.

lateNotes.anchor-point: The lanyard clips to the platform's own anchor before the platform rises, not to whatever happens to be in reach once it is already up.
lateNotes.platform-gate: The gate gets closed before the platform ever rises, not checked once the associate is already at height.

name: High-Bay Order Picker Fall Protection

passRule.note: stars >= 2 and no unsafe action (WebXR/shared/records.js passed())

steps.cue: Hi-vis vest and full-body harness before touching the picker.
steps.prompt: Hi-vis vest and full-body harness before touching the picker.
steps.title: Suit up before the pre-use check
steps.why: The harness only protects an associate who is already wearing it correctly before the platform ever leaves the ground — putting it on after the pre-use check, instead of before, is how a fitted strap gets skipped under time pressure.

steps.cue: Confirm today's pre-use tag on the picker before stepping onto the platform.
steps.prompt: Confirm today's pre-use tag on the picker before stepping onto the platform.
steps.title: Read the pre-use inspection tag
steps.why: The tag is the record that somebody already walked this specific truck today — riding the platform up without reading it means trusting a machine on nothing but how it looked from across the aisle.

steps.cue: Look the picker over before stepping on. Three things are already wrong with it — find them.

decoyNotes.intact-beacon: That beacon is mounted, wired and undamaged. Nothing to flag there.

itemNotes.frayed-lanyard-hazard: A lanyard with a frayed core strand gets tagged out, not clipped in — it goes to the crib, not onto anyone's harness.
itemNotes.gate-wedge-hazard: The wedge comes out before the gate is trusted to close on its own again.
itemNotes.missing-pin-hazard: An empty pin socket gets a pin before this guard is trusted to stay where it is bolted.

steps.prompt: Look the picker over before stepping on. Three things are already wrong with it — find them.
steps.title: Read the picker for what is already wrong with it
steps.why: A picker that looks fine from the aisle is not the same thing as one an associate has actually checked — a wedged gate, a frayed lanyard or a missing pin each quietly removes a fall-protection control, and finding them now costs a tag-out instead of costing someone the one time they needed the control that was not actually there.

steps.cue: Close the platform's own gate before the platform ever leaves the ground.
steps.prompt: Close the platform's own gate before the platform ever leaves the ground.
steps.title: Close the platform gate
steps.why: The gate is the one side of the platform rail built to open, and it only protects anyone once it is actually closed — checking it now, at ground level, is the last chance to fix it before it is a gap forty feet up.

steps.cue: Carry the lanyard's snap hook to the platform's own anchor point and clip it in before rising.

drag.missNote: Not on the platform's own anchor — the lanyard only does its job clipped to the point built to take the load.

steps.prompt: Carry the lanyard's snap hook to the platform's own anchor point and clip it in before rising.
steps.title: Clip the lanyard to the platform anchor
steps.why: The platform's own anchor is engineered to hold a fall-arrest load; a nearby rail or a convenient loop was not — clipping to the anchor specifically, not just to something within reach, is what makes the harness a fall-arrest system instead of a costume.

steps.cue: Hold the raise control until the platform reaches the marked picking height.
steps.holdBreakNote: Released the raise control before reaching picking height. A platform stopped partway between levels is a platform reaching distance that was never actually planned for.
steps.prompt: Hold the raise control until the platform reaches the marked picking height.
steps.title: Raise the platform to picking height
steps.why: Holding the raise control the whole way up, rather than bumping it in short presses, is what keeps the ascent smooth and predictable — a platform that lurches in stops and starts is a platform that can catch a foot that was braced for steady motion.

steps.cue: Read the height and load gauge and commit only inside the rated band.

gauge.label: HEIGHT / LOAD RATING
gauge.missNote: Committed outside the rated combination. Reduce the load or the height before reaching for the next case.

steps.prompt: Read the height and load gauge and commit only inside the rated band.
steps.title: Confirm height and load within rating
steps.why: A picker's rated capacity changes with how high the platform has gone, and the gauge is the only honest read of where this specific lift stands against that rating — reaching for one more case on the strength of how sturdy the platform feels is exactly the guess the gauge replaces.

steps.cue: Set the picker's brakes before reaching out from the platform.
steps.prompt: Set the picker's brakes before reaching out from the platform.
steps.title: Set the brakes
steps.why: A picker that can creep while an associate is leaning out from the platform turns a stable reach into a moving target — setting the brakes first is what keeps the platform exactly where it was raised.

steps.cue: Select the case marked on today's pick list from the rack.
steps.prompt: Select the case marked on today's pick list from the rack.
steps.title: Pick the marked case
steps.why: Picking the marked case rather than the nearest one is what keeps the warehouse management system's count honest — a substituted pick looks fine on this platform and shows up as a shortage three moves later, on somebody else's shift.

steps.cue: Lower the case onto the platform while keeping the load-moment indicator inside the centred band.
steps.holdBreakNote: The load moment drifted out of the centred band. Re-centre the case before continuing the transfer.
steps.prompt: Lower the case onto the platform while keeping the load-moment indicator inside the centred band.
steps.title: Transfer the case onto the platform
steps.why: Watching the load-moment indicator through the transfer is what catches a case being set down off-centre before it actually tips the platform's balance — a heavy case set down blind is a platform that finds out about the imbalance only once it starts to tilt.

steps.cue: Hold the lower control until the platform is fully back on the ground.
steps.holdBreakNote: Released the lower control before the platform was fully down. A platform stopped partway down is still a platform above the ground.
steps.prompt: Hold the lower control until the platform is fully back on the ground.
steps.title: Lower the platform to the ground
steps.why: Holding the descent all the way down, the same way the ascent was held, is what keeps this from being the platform that stops half-lowered while an associate already believes it is safe to move around on.

steps.cue: Unclip the lanyard from the platform anchor only once the platform is fully on the ground.
steps.prompt: Unclip the lanyard from the platform anchor only once the platform is fully on the ground.
steps.title: Unclip the lanyard
steps.why: The lanyard's whole job ends the moment the platform is back at ground level — unclipping any earlier, while the platform is still descending, is trading a fall-arrest connection for the belief that the descent will finish without incident.

steps.cue: Sign the pick log before moving on to the next aisle.
steps.prompt: Sign the pick log before moving on to the next aisle.
steps.title: Sign the pick log
steps.why: The signed log is the record that this specific pick, on this specific platform, actually followed the fall-protection sequence — not assumed fine because the associate usually does it right.

supportLine: your Teamsters local's member assistance programme, or the site's employee assistance line if a close call at height on an order picker is what stayed with you
tagline: Riding a stand-up order picker into the high bay the way its own fall-protection sequence requires: the gate closed before the platform rises, the harness clipped to the platform's own anchor, the height and load proven before reaching for stock, and the unclip saved for after the platform is back on the ground
